subject: Error generating empirical plot in vertical scaling (subscript out of bounds)

messages.author: 1a2399df702b526b
messages.subject: Error generating empirical plot in vertical scaling (subscript out of bounds)
parts:
Hello Phil,

I am performing vertical equating using the 'multipleGroup' function. My data follows a planned missing design, where some items were only answered by one of the groups, while anchor items were answered by both groups.

I would like to identify misfitting items. However, when I use the 'itemfit' function with the 'empirical.plot' argument, I am unable to generate empirical plots for items that have missing responses in one of the groups. Below is a reproducible example:


library(mirt)
set.seed(12345)

a <- matrix(abs(rnorm(15,1,.3)), ncol=1)
d <- matrix(rnorm(15,0,.7),ncol=1)
itemtype <- rep('2PL', nrow(a))
N <- 1000
dataset1 <- simdata(a, d, N, itemtype)
dataset2 <- simdata(a, d, N, itemtype, mu = .1, sigma = matrix(1.5))
dat <- rbind(dataset1, dataset2)
group <- c(rep('D1', N), rep('D2', N))

dat2 <- dat
dat2[group == 'D1', 1:2] <- dat2[group != 'D1', 14:15] <- NA
head(dat2)
tail(dat2)

# items with missing responses need to be constrained across groups for identification
nms <- colnames(dat2)
mod <- multipleGroup(dat2, 1, group, invariance = nms[c(1:2, 14:15)])

# Empirical plot
itemfit(
  mod,
  empirical.plot = 1,
  Theta = as.numeric(fscores(mod, method = "EAP"))
  )
 
Error in empirical.plot_points[1, ] : subscript out of bounds


Is there any way to generate the empirical plot for items with NA in one of the groups? If not, what alternative approach could I use to check for misfit in items with missing data in one of the groups?

messages.author: b330c2028fed415b
messages.subject: Re: Error generating empirical plot in vertical scaling (subscript out of bounds)
parts:
This looks to be a bug, but a predictable one. You really can't build an empirical plot for a given item when all the responses within a group are NAs. It should however be possible to take a group subset via extract.group() and plot the items that way....

Phil
